references.text: Describes the holy garments made for Aaron, which were later to be inherited by his sons.
Concerns the garments of Aaron's sons and their priestly service.
Moses clothes Aaron and his sons with the holy garments and anoints them for priestly service.
Describes how Aaron was clothed in the holy priestly garments during the consecration ceremony.
Moses anoints Aaron and his sons with anointing oil to set them apart as holy.
Refers to the holy garments that the high priest was to wear.
Aaron's garments were taken from him and placed on his son Eleazar, showing the inheritance of the priestly garments.
Mentions the anointing of Aaron's sons for priestly service.
Refers to the eternal priesthood order passed down to descendants.
Connects the ordination ritual itself with the subsequent succession of the priestly service.
Explains the ritual (blood and oil) that makes the garments holy enough to be inherited.
